Juvenile Streamlined spinefoot, Siganus argenteus, recruit to nearshore seagrass beds after a pelagic larval phase lasting several weeks. Upon settlement, they exhibit a distinctive silvery flank with fine blue lines, a pattern that gradually shifts towards the adult colouration as they grow. The onset of sexual maturation is tied closely to body size, with individuals typically attaining puberty once they reach a total length of approximately 22 cm [Lp = approximately 22 cm], a size that corresponds to a wet weight of around 146 grams [Wwp = around 146 grams] based on established length-weight relationships for this species. These values indicate that a substantial portion of somatic growth occurs before the reproductive system becomes active. Newly hatched larvae, emerging from pelagic eggs with a diameter of roughly 0.65 mm, possess a minute wet weight at birth of about 0.00014 grams [Wwb = about 0.00014 grams], reflecting the limited yolk reserves available to the endotrophic larva during the brief interval before first exogenous feeding. This extremely small initial mass imposes a high vulnerability to starvation during the early planktonic stages.

The reproductive biology of Siganus argenteus has been investigated through field collections of gravid individuals across the species' range in the tropical Indo-Pacific. Ovarian histology reveals that females undergo at least two distinct spawning events per year, and the gonadosomatic index (GSI) averages approximately 10% [GSI = approximately 10%] when measured under ambient summer water temperatures near 27.8 °C [T = 27.8 °C]. The index reflects the mass of the ripe ovaries relative to the total body mass, providing a snapshot of the instantaneous reproductive allocation for a spawning-capable female. Of particular note, the condition of the gonads deteriorates rapidly after each spawning bout, with the GSI declining sharply before rebuilding for the subsequent batch.

Mature adults of this siganid reach a maximum recorded total length of approximately 40 cm [Li = approximately 40 cm], a size that is among the larger members of the genus Siganus. At this ultimate length, individuals can achieve a corresponding ultimate wet weight of roughly 871.6 grams [Wwi = roughly 871.6 grams], a calculation derived from the allometric scaling relationship typical of the family. This asymptotic body mass suggests that growth slows considerably once the fish approach this ceiling, with most energetic resources being diverted towards gamete production and somatic maintenance rather than further length increase. Field surveys in the Philippines and northern Australia have documented large, old individuals that appear to have reached this plateau, their growth curves nearly flat over the final years of life. The substantial size range from the 0.00014 gram hatchling to the 871.6 gram adult underscores a dramatic ontogenetic increase spanning six orders of magnitude in mass.

Longevity estimates for the Streamlined spinefoot are based on mark-recapture studies and otolith increment analysis conducted in coral reef environments where water temperatures remain relatively stable year-round. The maximum documented lifespan under natural conditions in warm tropical waters at approximately 27.8 °C [T = 27.8 °C] is near three years [am = three years], a comparatively short life history for a fish of this size. This relatively compressed lifespan highlights a fast-paced life strategy, with rapid juvenile growth, early maturation at a moderate body size, and high annual reproductive output. In contrast to longer-lived reef herbivores like some parrotfishes, Siganus argenteus appears to channel energy into early and repeated reproduction rather than extended somatic persistence. The interplay between the three-year maximum age and the biannual spawning schedule suggests that a typical female may participate in only a handful of reproductive seasons during her lifetime, placing a premium on the success of each egg batch.

Comparative studies with other siganid species reveal an interesting trade-off in life-history architecture among the rabbitfishes. The Streamlined spinefoot attains puberty at a total length of 22 cm [Lp = 22 cm], which is proportionally larger relative to its ultimate length of 40 cm [Li = 40 cm] than in the closely related Siganus fuscescens. This delayed onset of maturity relative to maximum body size may be a consequence of its more pelagic foraging habits, which require a larger body to sustain the higher metabolic demands of cruising in open water. The ultimate wet weight of 871.6 grams [Wwi = 871.6 grams] places it among the moderately sized members of the genus, and the wet weight at puberty of 146 grams [Wwp = 146 grams] indicates that roughly 17 percent of the asymptotic mass is achieved before any investment in gonadal tissue begins. Future work examining these life-history parameters across a latitudinal gradient, particularly at the edges of the species' thermal range, would clarify the extent to which temperature modulates the growth and reproductive schedule.
